title: Add TermAl-managed AutoApprove for Codex
outcome: Codex approvalPolicy=never is a native app-server policy that suppresses prompts and lets sandbox-denied operations fail; it is not equivalent to Claude's TermAl-managed AutoApprove. Add a distinct auto-approve Codex mode so TermAl requests native on-request approvals and answers eligible approval requests automatically. This also fixes orchestrator autoApprove=true currently mapping Codex to Never.
acceptance: The auto-approve value round-trips through persistence, API, remote snapshots, settings UI, slash palette, and docs while Never remains distinct and remains the default. Codex receives native on-request for auto-approve at thread start/resume and turn start. During a turn whose active policy is AutoApprove, TermAl immediately accepts commandExecution, fileChange, and permissions approval requests once/turn using existing response shapes, without creating approval cards or pending entries. User input, MCP elicitation, and generic app requests remain interactive. Active read-only delegation children always receive exact decline-shaped responses for all three approval kinds, including Windows reviewers using danger-full-access. A mid-turn settings change does not alter the active turn policy. Orchestrator template autoApprove=true maps Codex to AutoApprove; delegation children remain initially forced to Never. Focused and full Rust/UI gates pass, followed by independent Fable verification.
